ud8.4:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud8.4:1.3: o Then at that time the Fortunate One was instructing, rousing, enthusing, and cheering the monks with a Dhamma talk connected with Emancipation. Those monks, after making it their goal, applying their minds,
ud8.4:1.4: considering it with all their mind, were listening to Dhamma with an attentive ear.
ud8.4:2.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud8.4:3.1: “For the dependent there is agitation, for the independent there is no agitation.
ud8.4:3.3: When there is no agitation there is calm, when there is calm there is no inclining.
ud8.4:3.4: When there is no inclining, there is no coming or going.
ud8.4:3.5: When there is no coming or going, there is no passing away and rebirth.
ud8.4:3.6: When there is no passing away and rebirth, there is no here or hereafter or in between the two
ud8.4:3.7: - just this is the end of suffering.”
